He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Information & Risk Disclosure Any discussion of securities, assets, or financial markets in this email is for informational context only and does not represent investment guidance of any kind. We have 10 days to power Ruwa Romman to victory — this race is hers to win.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260607-1&t=1&akid=3570%2E587540%2E6MHwRO)
Peter,
**A couple weeks ago, Ruwa Romman came out on top in a four-way Democratic primary for Georgia’s 7th State Senate District.**
Now she’s headed into a runoff on **June 16** — and we need your support to get her across the finish line.
Ruwa has been absolutely _crushing it_ on the campaign trail. In just under 60 days leading up to her primary, she and her team knocked thousands of doors and made tens of thousands of calls. And despite being outspent 3-to-1, Ruwa received more votes than _any Democratic primary candidate in the history of this district._
Ruwa has built a campaign that has what it takes to go toe-to-toe with big money. And she did it by showing up, building real relationships in her community, and running the kind of grassroots campaign that the people of Gwinnett County actually connected with.
That’s who Ruwa is. That’s who she’s always been.
**[If you’re ready to help power Ruwa to victory on June 16, will you split a $5 donation between Ruwa’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve right now?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260607_1_ruwa.zbgVzB&refcode=em20260607-3570&amount=5&t=2&akid=3570%2E587540%2E6MHwRO)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260607_1_ruwa.zbgVzB&amount=5&refcode=em20260607-3570&t=3&akid=3570%2E587540%2E6MHwRO)**
Since making history in 2022 as the first Muslim woman and first Palestinian American elected to public office in Georgia, Ruwa has been fighting like hell for her district.
She **introduced the first statewide data center moratorium in the entire country** — because she understands that data centers are draining water supplies and skyrocketing Georgia Power bills in communities that never got a say in those decisions.
She **secured $50 million for Gwinnett County road improvements**. She fought to **lower property taxes without cutting a single dollar from school funding**. And right now, as Republican-dominated legislatures are rushing to draw racist gerrymandered maps in their favor, Ruwa is on the frontlines of that fight as a member of the Georgia House Democratic Caucus redistricting team.
Peter, this is a safe blue seat. It’s not an exaggeration to say that **winning the runoff on June 16 means winning the seat in November.**
This runoff in District 7 is a chance to send a leader to the Gold Dome who has already shown that she’ll fight for them. She’s got the track record and ties to the community to prove it.
What Ruwa needs right now, in the final 10 days before her election, is grassroots support from folks like you to help her finish this race strong.
The last runoff we had in Georgia was to support Akbar Ali who won by just 153 votes. This one could be even closer. **So any support you can send to Ruwa in this final stretch could be the deciding factor in this race.**
**[Will you split a $5 donation between Ruwa’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260607_1_ruwa.zbgVzB&refcode=em20260607-3570&amount=5&t=4&akid=3570%2E587540%2E6MHwRO)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Our democracy is not a commodity to be sold to the highest bidder.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260607-6324-footer&t=1&akid=6324%2E420207%2EJhVFCP)
**Our democracy is not a commodity to be sold to the highest bidder, Peter.**
But since the passage of _Citizens United_ over 15 years ago, that’s exactly what it's become — and working families have had to bear the weight of it ever since.
We feel it every single day. At the gas pump, in the grocery store, at their doctor’s office. We watch our priorities get buried beneath a sea of dark money. Then we see the same corporations buying influence in our elections write the rules shaping our daily lives.
This is completely unacceptable. Working people deserve better.
Since my very first days in Congress, I have been proud to lead the charge to overturn _Citizens United_ and I won’t stop fighting until we get big money out of politics.
Last month, Hawaii made history becoming the first state in the country to sign a bill into law that strips corporations of the power to spend in their state’s politics entirely. That’s proof our movement is building — and it’s proof that this fight can be won.
It’s time to reverse this ruling, bring trust and transparency back into our government, and put power back into the hands of working people.
[**Will you add your name to this petition to demand Congress rein in corporate power and overturn _Citizens United_?** ](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260607-end-citizens-united/?source=em20260607-6324&t=2&akid=6324%2E420207%2EJhVFCP)

name: Carrie Walter
subject: It's Jeff's Birthday — Can You Help Me Surprise Him?
body:
| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Friends,
Today is Jeff’s birthday.
As his wife, I’ve had the privilege of watching him wear many hats over the years—husband, father, friend, business owner, community leader, and now candidate for Congress.
What I’ve always admired most about Jeff is that he genuinely cares about people. Whether he’s helping a neighbor, supporting a local organization, or listening to concerns from families across our district, he approaches every challenge with the same commitment: finding solutions and making a difference.
Running for Congress hasn’t been easy. It means long days, late nights, missed family dinners, and countless miles on the road meeting voters. But Jeff believes our community deserves strong leadership and a representative who will fight for hardworking families.
That’s why I’m reaching out today.
Instead of asking you to send Jeff a birthday card, I’m asking if you’ll consider making a birthday contribution to his campaign.
Whether it’s $25, $50, $100, or any amount you’re able to give, your support will help our campaign reach more voters, grow our grassroots efforts, and build the organization needed to win.
I know Jeff would never ask for anything for himself on his birthday. That’s one of the many reasons I love him.
But I also know how much it would mean to him to see people stepping up to support the campaign and the mission that has become such an important part of our family’s life.
If you’ve been thinking about getting involved or making a contribution, today would be the perfect day.
Together, we can give Jeff the best birthday gift possible: the resources needed to continue building a winning campaign.
Thank you for your friendship, support, and belief in Jeff’s vision for our district.
Warmly,
Carrie Walter
P.S. I’d love to tell Jeff that supporters from across the district helped us reach a special birthday fundraising goal today. Will you make a contribution and help us celebrate his birthday by investing in the future of this campaign?

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Friends, Today is Jeff’s birthday. As his wife, I’ve had the privilege of watching him wear many hats over the years—husband, father, friend, business owner, community leader, and now candidate for Congress. Running for Congress hasn’t been easy. It means long days, late nights, missed family dinners, and countless miles on the road meeting voters. Why Jennifer Granholm's support means so much to me

| |
---|---|---

# [This endorsement is personal](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=200774259&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAwNzc0MjU5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODA4NTU2MTEsImV4cCI6MTc4MzQ0NzYxMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.cAqLcw8kiJViR0zhlK5DHoM0EA5OKj6rNpDxKvx3Ql0)
### Why Jennifer Granholm's support means so much to me
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jun 7
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL3RoaXMtZW5kb3JzZW1lbnQtaXMtcGVyc29uYWw_.iuek_bNXzdfiWrPP4e2R-pzDBimzwA2GyndgkqxGfHE?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/this-endorsement-is-personal?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

I wanted to make sure you saw our big news: Former Michigan Governor Jennifer Granholm has endorsed me for the U.S. Senate.
I have to say, this one is especially meaningful.
I first worked with Governor Granholm during one of the hardest stretches our state has ever been through: It was 2009. The country was in a recession. The auto industry was on the brink. Plants were shutting down. And Michiganders were wondering if their jobs - and the only industry many of their families had ever worked for - would survive.
The anxiety, fear, and uncertainty were palpable across our state.
I was working as Chief of Staff to President Obama's auto rescue, and Governor Granholm was leading Michigan through the crisis from Lansing. From those two ends, we worked together to help save 200,000 jobs in Michigan.
I will never forget that time. I'll never forget what it felt like to fight tooth and nail to give people hope again. And I will never forget Governor Granholm's incredible leadership.
What I remember most about her in that moment is that she never once lost sight of the real Michiganders we were fighting for.
It was not just an economic crisis. There were livelihoods on the line. And she knew it.
She knew the names of the businesses, the towns, and the communities that would be hollowed out if a factory closed. She knew what was at stake for workers and families. And when the cameras turned away, she was still working - early in the morning and late into the night - for Michigan.
That is the kind of leader she is. She is Michigan grit. So when she said this about me last month, I was deeply honored:
> "Michigan's next Senator needs to focus on Michigan jobs, Michigan manufacturing, bringing down costs for Michigan families and standing up for Michigan against Donald Trump's recklessness. That's Haley Stevens. Haley's got Michigan grit, which I saw while she served as Chief of Staff to President Obama's auto rescue and was a key member of the team that helped save 200,000 Michigan auto jobs."
It's special when someone you've stood shoulder to shoulder with during an extremely difficult time says: I've seen Haley in action. She has what it takes.
That's why this endorsement is special.
Because Governor Granholm is not somebody who hands out endorsements lightly. She has seen the inside of an economic crisis from the governor's office and the inside of a Cabinet department in Washington. She knows the difference between a candidate who can do the job and one who is just running to get rich or famous.
And she is standing with me because she believes Michigan is worth fighting for. So do I.
Her endorsement also tells me something I've already been feeling on the ground: This campaign is about the things that matter most. Fighting for Michiganders. For Michigan jobs. For Michigan manufacturing. Bringing down costs for Michigan families who are struggling to afford the basics. And standing up to a president whose chaos keeps costing Michigan real money and real opportunity.
That's the work.
That's why I'm running.
And that's why Governor Granholm is with us.
I'm sure I don't have to remind you that Senate control runs through Michigan. The polls show I'm the strongest Democrat to defeat Mike Rogers, and having Governor Granholm with us tells the entire political world that we can win.
Jennifer Granholm spent eight years showing Michigan what a fighter looks like. Then she spent four more showing the country what Michigan grit looks like from a president's Cabinet.
To have her on our team is a huge honor.
Thank you, Governor Granholm.
I'm more fired up than ever.
Let's keep working.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/bd2d7263-aa36-4df0-b3c0-b3d502a0999e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Peter,
Before we get to this week's story, a moment of thanks. Your generosity through our end-of-month push made a huge impact.
And what's next is big: We're putting hundreds volunteers in the field to knock on thousands of doors for our Weekend of Action, June 20–21.
Want to be one of them? We're hosting an informational call Monday at 5 p.m. CDT for anyone who wants to help. No experience needed — just bring yourself.

_"I met Fran at a Citizen Action meeting. I was impressed that she was so thoughtful and passionate about the issues faced by Wisconsinites._
_My main issues are healthcare access and affordability. I'm a retired physician who heard countless stories of struggle from people over 40 years of practice and volunteering to serve the uninsured. It's now the number one issue of affordability, according to polling of Americans._
_She's a bright, hardworking person who has struggled with the common issues of being a single mom and a business owner trying to make ends meet. She has lived this, like millions of others."_
**— Steven Manson, La Crosse**
* * *
Wisconsin families pay some of the highest hospital prices in the country while insurance companies get rich denying their claims. As governor, Fran will rein in what the biggest hospital systems can charge. She'll build a public option so everyone can afford coverage. And she'll force insurers to justify every claim they deny — because getting sick shouldn't bankrupt you.
We're so grateful for supporters like Steven, and we'll never stop fighting for fairer, cheaper healthcare.

He carried the nuclear football for President Obama — now he's running as a Democrat to flip Michigan's 7th congressional district. If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | Team, over $25 million in ad spending has been reserved in MI-07’s House race. We knew this would be one of the most expensive races in the nation. That matters most now. Early voting BEGINS in UNDER A MONTH, we have to pick up our fundraising in order to keep up. That seems like a lot, but if everyone who received an email from us in May chipped in $25 we’d have all the resources we need to push back against this massive spending. But the harsh truth is, not everyone gives. 99% of the people who read this will look the other way. We’re hoping you’re part of the 1% willing to lean in and demand better out of this moment. | Michigan’s 7th district is expected to be the deciding factor in flipping the House. That’s why dark money is pouring in from billionaires, and corporations around the country to re-elect Tom Barrett. We can’t let that happen. Maasdam is running for Congress to help get money out of politics. Corporations and secret donors should never have been allowed to spend unlimited sums of money to buy candidates. But Matt hasn’t taken a cent from corporate PACs. Team, we know you can’t give every time, but right now, we need you. Votes will be cast this month, and we have an official FEC deadline on the 30th. ---|---|---
The protein boom is alive and well. Unless you live under a rock, you've likely seen protein being marketed on almost every food item you buy. [Doritos](https://substack.com/redirect/5ace938c-9138-4ff6-8a5b-f503bf64b3f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), your [coffee](https://substack.com/redirect/1e654dc3-2a9c-4f0e-be68-c9ac13b65324?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and even your [ice cream](https://substack.com/redirect/c3b7f045-a45c-460d-a3df-741792249417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) now trumpet their protein content. And it's not just a marketing story; consumers are demanding more protein. [A majority of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/8c6641ce-6cf0-424f-bbc0-515c9b913c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) say they're actively trying to eat more of it. Meat snacks alone have become a [$5.5 billion juggernaut](https://substack.com/redirect/8c6641ce-6cf0-424f-bbc0-515c9b913c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and #protein[ has millions of posts on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/c3524a63-3363-4da0-a8df-f714f6934e64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). These days, the word "protein" on a package is almost as important as the price.
Food fads are not new, and while I believe the protein story isn't a fleeting phenomenon, it's not unreasonable to question the sustainability of the boom. After all, before protein, American consumers were infatuated with hydration. Remember when Liquid I.V. suddenly appeared everywhere? When everyone started carrying water bottles and Stanley cups became a status symbol?
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..KQz6pYaiYOekROTfr7wSuesNeb-7SAYI5CwWPrDXAss?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=200931809)
It seems to me there's a pattern here. First, a real health concept goes mainstream, social media amplifies interest in the topic, the food industry builds an empire with brands and products to help consumers achieve their goals, our culture changes to incorporate the new desires, and suddenly it's in every aisle of your grocery store.
For the past eighteen months, I've had a front row seat as food trends play out in real time. Regular readers will know that I currently run a private-label frozen pizza company that produces single-serve offerings for some of the largest grocers in America.
As the protein wave rapidly accelerated and gained momentum (even before Starbucks and Dunkin' had amplified the interest) in early 2025, I directed my product development team to focus their efforts on a high-protein pizza. Early last fall, our taste tests indicated we had a winner, and the market agreed. One of America's largest grocery retailers agreed to put it on its shelves in 2026.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c088eaef-55dd-4d1e-8f13-02a5d3a528cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I say this not to sell you pizza but to explain why I spend an unusual amount of time studying food trends, how consumer focus interfaces with market opportunities, and, perhaps most importantly, what might be coming next. And in that regard, I've been directing our innovation efforts at Goodwell Foods towards what I believe may be an even bigger trend than protein.
And those running the biggest food companies in the world seem to agree with me as they too are saying the F-word.
**Fiber**.
Bigger than protein? Yes. How's that? Turns out that most Americans already get enough protein. [Johns Hopkins](https://substack.com/redirect/3868938f-b65c-47b3-b2bd-ccb5fe106c3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) puts it simply: "Americans get plenty of protein, but not enough fiber." The numbers aren't even close. According to the [American Society of Nutrition](https://substack.com/redirect/3406824c-72f4-4320-8ba1-8e2bc36fc1d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), around **7% of American adults** consume the recommended daily fiber. [Over 90% of women and 97% of men fall short](https://substack.com/redirect/546aef76-ed47-4e2c-9666-251b9cd81f46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the recommended 25 to 35 grams per day.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e4ba7d93-6b05-44a3-a88d-03ccc10ed7c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The opportunity is enormous. The average American gets about 15 grams of fiber a day, about half of what they need. That's like eating a single apple and not consuming any additional fiber all day. Most foods (pasta, a sandwich, a bag of chips, a protein bar) don't even move the needle. Those foods that do (beans, lentils, vegetables, whole grains) have been scraped off American plates by low-carb dieting efforts and our (relatively) newfound protein obsession. We spent years telling people to avoid carbs. Fiber was the baby thrown out with the bathwater.
Nearly everyone in America is skipping the indigestible carbohydrate that fights heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, while also providing necessary fuel for our gut microbiome, which is connected to everything from our immune system to our moods. Fiber, it turns out, may be the biggest nutritional deficiency we've discovered yet and has the potential to mitigate numerous chronic diseases.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/317b5155-c87f-478e-9a99-e2dc2e0fb471?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But could this be a fleeting trend that never makes it into the mainstream? To validate my thinking, I often turn to the people whose bonuses depend on figuring out these trends. On a recent earnings call, for instance, PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta boldly noted that ["fiber will be the next protein."](https://substack.com/redirect/546aef76-ed47-4e2c-9666-251b9cd81f46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) And McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski [publicly predicted](https://substack.com/redirect/cfd98373-27de-4222-be51-66d1831e6742?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that fiber "is going to be big." When the leaders ofPepsiCo and McDonald's both say the same thing, I pay attention.
And the signals are now rapidly emerging. PepsiCo is launching [Smartfood Fiber Pop and SunChips Fiber](https://substack.com/redirect/a2632862-fa00-48ee-b4d5-1f61377c04d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Whole Foods put fiber-forward products in its [2026 trend forecast](https://substack.com/redirect/546aef76-ed47-4e2c-9666-251b9cd81f46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Thrive Market reported a **30% surge** in fiber-related search terms. And [Datassential](https://substack.com/redirect/a2632862-fa00-48ee-b4d5-1f61377c04d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the food research firm that tracks what's actually moving in the industry, called fiber "the next big health trend following on the heels of protein."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/262f5a66-52f8-41a2-b2b8-abd6bf90c4fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The validation from food industry titans tells me that fiber isn't just a fun speculation. The breadth of interest suggests there's an entire supply chain gearing up to feed a forthcoming surge in American appetites for fiber.
[GLP-1 drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/245af8c4-0730-47d3-abbd-5f7b08ea2f6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are further accelerating this trend. About [one in five American adults](https://substack.com/redirect/07239cd0-ecd0-4d64-9086-d31e2b331bba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have used (or are using) Ozempic, Wegovy, or a similar medication. GLP-1 users experience a [25 to 40 percent decrease in caloric intake](https://substack.com/redirect/cfe81561-07a2-4784-b22e-2fef6bdef525?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which means every bite has to count. Nutrient density per calorie increasingly matters. Given its ability to deliver satiety, blood sugar stability, and gut health, fiber demand is likely to rise rapidly alongside GLP usage. When the drugs that are reshaping how America eats also happen to increase the need for fiber, you have a trend with structural tailwinds, not just a viral TikTok moment.
Speaking of TikTok, social media has jumped aboard with "[Fibermaxxing](https://substack.com/redirect/cfd98373-27de-4222-be51-66d1831e6742?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," the act of maximizing daily fiber intake through every meal and snack. Fibermaxxing started online, moved into mainstream food culture, and is now in the boardrooms of America's largest food companies. [A majority of consumers](https://substack.com/redirect/cfd98373-27de-4222-be51-66d1831e6742?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said they'd try "fibermaxxing" after learning about it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fde55d08-31ff-493f-8db3-09be0672702d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Every few years, the food industry finds a health trend to rally around. Hydration had its moment. Protein is today's focus. And, I really believe that fiber is next. When 93% of the country isn't getting enough of something that prevents heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, that's not a trend. That's an opportunity. And a big market.
The CEOs of the largest companies in the world are placing their bets. Product launches are already in motion. Social media is abuzz with discussion. And back in our test kitchen at Goodwell Foods, our product development team is working on developing a high-fiber pizza that will be ready to go later this year.
Soon, everyone will be saying the F word.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7b058170-a448-48f5-934f-c58b1bd5a970?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI** is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. **He 's currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza**. _LinkedIn_ has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and _Worth_ profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, _**[The Making of a Generalist: An Independent Thinker Finds Unconventional Success in an Uncertain World](https://substack.com/redirect/ef8b7309-b061-4937-a777-88af21cb6924?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ , _**[Think for Yourself: Restoring Common Sense in an Age of Experts and Artificial Intelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/f84ccf12-f573-4ddf-bb55-41d7d61ec374?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ and _**[Boombustology: Spotting Financial Bubbles Before They Burst](https://substack.com/redirect/ff34c451-a4a0-49db-8bf1-f0310f4938da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_. Vikram lives in Lincoln, New Hampshire with his wife and two children, where they can usually be found hiking or skiing.

Peter,

Kurt Alme won the Republican primary.

And before the votes were even fully counted, the Democrat machine was already making moves.

That is how much they want this seat. Chuck Schumer knows that Montana is the key to flipping the Senate. He has unlimited dark money, out-of-state donors, and a playbook designed to defeat Kurt before November.

Here is what they are up against.

Kurt is a Montana native who has lived all over this state. He is a former U.S. Attorney, twice nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate. He cut Montana's taxes, balanced our budget, and prosecuted the violent criminals and drug traffickers threatening our families.

President Trump endorsed Kurt early because he knows what Kurt is capable of.

But none of that matters if we can't match the Democrats’ fundraising machine in this race.

Right now, in the first few days after the primary, we need to show the country that Montana grassroots conservatives are ready to fight. A strong fundraising number this week tells Schumer and the left that Montana is not for sale.

name: Chris Pappas
subject: I never imagined this future was possible
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Growing up gay in New Hampshire, I never imagined this future was
possible.

While I was lucky to receive love and support from family and friends, it
was still hard to picture a time when I would be able to live openly let
alone be elected to Congress.

I certainly never imagined the community I grew up in would embrace me,
believe in me, and elect me to represent them — not just once, but four
times in a row.

We can’t
change hearts, minds, or laws without a seat at the table. I’m running for
Senate to represent all Granite Staters. And while, if elected, I would be
the first out gay man in the Senate, my campaign is really about lowering
costs, protecting health care access, and standing up to a reckless Trump
Administration, especially as they attack the LGBTQ+ community.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260607_2.H43U-2&refcode=em20260607-2&t=1003&akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC ]So,
will you help me stand up for all Granite Staters? Pitch in
$5 to support my grassroots campaign.

When I came out there were examples of LGBTQ+ trailblazers — like Harvey
Milk — who had been elected to public office, but it wasn’t a very long
list.

With the support of my community, I became the first out gay man to
represent New Hampshire in Congress back in 2018. I defeated the GOP four
times in one of the swingiest districts in the country. Now I’m fighting
to keep our U.S. Senate seat blue.

New Hampshire is one of the most critical swing states in this election
cycle. Republicans are targeting this race, aiming to flip this
competitive seat red and expand their majority.

But we’re going to stop them together – just like we’ve done before. We’re
going to keep this seat blue, and we’re going to defy expectations when we
take back the Senate.

This campaign means so much. It’s something that my
younger self would never have even imagined. And not only is this race our
opportunity to make history, but it’s also a crucial election we can’t
afford to lose to the GOP. The stakes are simply too high.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260607_2.H43U-2&refcode=em20260607-2&t=1004&akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC ]If it makes sense for you today, please make a $5
contribution to my campaign.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260607_2.H43U-2&amount=5&refcode=em20260607-2&t=1023&akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC ]Donate $5 »

Happy Pride Month.

And thank you — as always — for your kindness and support.

With gratitude,

Chris

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=7067%2E582294%2EHLPSTC

| Peter,

There are only 16 days left until Election Day. And this week, **early voting begins.**

Right now, our team is working around the clock to reach every voter we can. We're knocking doors. Making calls. Running ads. Organizing volunteers. Talking to residents in every corner of the county.

Because campaigns like this are a marathon. _But these final days are also a sprint._

Montgomery County voters deserve the facts. They deserve to know about Andrew's record of fighting against tax increases, protecting homeowners, supporting public safety, and delivering results for our community.

These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

clean_body: This is happening faster than we can keep up | | | | | Patriot, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." body:
https://emergeamerica.org/ [https://emergeamerica.org/]
Friends,
Last weekend, Emerge President & CEO A'shanti Gholar was in South Carolina for Democratic Weekend, joining leaders, activists, and supporters at the Blue Palmetto Dinner, Congressman Jim Clyburn's World Famous Fish Fry, and the South Carolina Democratic Party Convention.
We also hosted an Emerge happy hour, bringing together alums, supporters, and Democrats from across the state. The energy was undeniable.
And that's important, because South Carolina reminds us why Emerge's work matters.
Just weeks ago, a redistricting battle threatened fair representation in the state. Had things gone differently, Congressman Jim Clyburn's seat could have been among those impacted. At the same time, more than 156,000 South Carolinians have already cast ballots in this year's primaries. Nearly 70% of those voters are Democrats — levels of engagement the state hasn't seen in decades.
People are paying attention. They're ready for change.
And Emerge women are stepping up to lead it.
We recently graduated another outstanding class of Emerge South Carolina women, and many of them are already on the ballot, running to serve their communities and fight for a stronger future.
That's why we remain committed to every one of our Emerge states. We're not retreating from difficult places. We're not giving up on communities that have been overlooked. And we're certainly not giving up on the South.
Because when women run, communities win. And when Democratic women have the training, support, and network they need, they can compete — and win — anywhere.
Will you help us continue building the bench in South Carolina and across the country with a contribution today?
secure.actblue.com/donate/emerge-2026-email?refcode=6-7 [secure.actblue.com/donate/emerge-2026-email?refcode=6-7]
The future of our democracy depends on leaders who reflect the communities they serve. Thanks to supporters like you, Emerge is helping make that future possible.
Thank you,
Ashley - Proud S. Carolinian

Peter, Memphis is worth fighting for. [Local news](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/8vGBl1ye2B2DUODM4sB4UQ~~/AAUS1hA~/qVyKboTAa9vJJe9HaI8-ujWNa_t97HUoN_a8sbdcX1alhb_7plYAlOjbD6dR-g2ExCRLIz_YFULmTVsQbw1_Enm59oCuFtrcxdr-rt48-7hym_P_TIwXYtYT_dL7Yig1al6-2D-5CzVsTZKsVqe0v_z30y97LDz1V-cMTzgDNniy0ra-5ZLS7gNtTfagsJ8KrGjBzxx_22gI0feuaKQAOxf9ToVw9OadJGV5YT6MU5ZjD3kbaKlv6qX7OEfi4vdD) in Memphis is starting to take notice of this race, and I want to make sure every voter in Shelby County hears directly from me. This gerrymandering was a slap in the face to Memphis voters. Memphis was the target, and the politicians in Nashville made no effort to hide it. They carved up Shelby County into three different congressional districts and called it a day. But here is what they did not count on: they handed Memphis an opportunity to send a message to the legislature, to Andy Ogles, and to anyone else paying attention, that this city is just as much a part of Tennessee as anywhere else in this state. Andy Ogles said he has "a lot more to learn" about Memphis. I have spent my entire career learning from communities like Memphis. As mayor of Columbia, I have had a front row seat to the issues that actually matter to people. And here is what I keep coming back to: the legislature can change the maps, but they cannot change the issues. Gas at over four dollars a gallon hits everyone. Unaffordable healthcare hits everyone. Tariffs hurting small businesses hit everyone. Those problems do not stop at congressional district lines, and neither will I. And, by the way, I happen to know Memphis pretty well already. clean_body: I want every voter in Shelby County to hear this directly from me. | | | | | Peter, Memphis is worth fighting for. in Memphis is starting to take notice of this race, and I want to make sure every voter in Shelby County hears directly from me. This gerrymandering was a slap in the face to Memphis voters. Memphis was the target, and the politicians in Nashville made no effort to hide it. They carved up Shelby County into three different congressional districts and called it a day. But here is what they did not count on: they handed Memphis an opportunity to send a message to the legislature, to Andy Ogles, and to anyone else paying attention, that this city is just as much a part of Tennessee as anywhere else in this state. Andy Ogles said he has "a lot more to learn" about Memphis. I have spent my entire career learning from communities like Memphis. As mayor of Columbia, I have had a front row seat to the issues that actually matter to people. And here is what I keep coming back to: the legislature can change the maps, but they cannot change the issues. Gas at over four dollars a gallon hits everyone. Unaffordable healthcare hits everyone. Tariffs hurting small businesses hit everyone. Those problems do not stop at congressional district lines, and neither will I. body:
Peter,

I just officially filed to run, and it's because of people like you that we've
made it this far.

I've been thinking about what I'd say when this day finally came.

I've been in this arena before. I know what a Senate campaign feels like. I

body:

---
| | Patriot,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=3beed891c2a140fba52663d2e4c771db&_e=hsFfoH86FbFauDLqY88TtpImgEnmJoMmWcrgA-KUCo53DkkLDAl4z2hpXXIKJDJjZVhSXTm1G1IC_6_YDktZJqI775qIDtTXljsjDkOjlb4FRH09PpmlT3pJifWOqMwm1kMSORhj09wR9GHyYnrE6_HC7gxAed4s4qmrIqOhjgZGvpTJt6xBo_xf2fAhNoiN2Pf13cERYXXRlUL01_1NwauizsHp9NTcHhc6-rTq6-p3b0PLHUNGqNv95UcHE23UmOmoFZlEbX4tRNwmaJknU0DdnXutBGBkabF1Z4WziUl4RigypLPHhU3J8NOMxmSRcUeKQgrmpbSs58N3_2Sre3xRL7kEFOrq-Ym5CV4DzaFONYlV_-9hDCeIDTiaQaCUvecJioirRQHR7PJUgDtqLm8wI2WDNl8zxKd6GxGhARKuNh1pT2dkFo_dxDr8GC0NrvLFZA4PJ9fMGTOahY7J87q_vUfDRxVfxbHhYXbqcDzWAnGC9nmt305b6soHXUQg6HmNeA9R9CrNbCoe6iPJkrIUvBMNBwvSt0XLlvQJbPXXzQkhm16cHiY110Cq16qXx999lWOguQesZWPrjF4fh-FMbCSswbmkOGCaD8AFr83n2DpExA154C2MSE9eQ4PxTWdGBRTS2eV9hn7MwtV4bvr6SZDJwnAmHiRI6K0bWfxat6MA2wBM_60194If7VjnO5xnnKn4kFFyBhebbNtKMw%3D%3D)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=3beed891c2a140fba52663d2e4c771db&_e=hsFfoH86FbFauDLqY88TtpImgEnmJoMmWcrgA-KUCo53DkkLDAl4z2hpXXIKJDJjZVhSXTm1G1IC_6_YDktZJqI775qIDtTXljsjDkOjlb4FRH09PpmlT3pJifWOqMwm1kMSORhj09wR9GHyYnrE6_HC7gxAed4s4qmrIqOhjgZGvpTJt6xBo_xf2fAhNoiN2Pf13cERYXXRlUL01_1NwauizsHp9NTcHhc6-rTq6-p3b0PLHUNGqNv95UcHE23UctB_KKr-t1uj2cCrhfLoi4wSQ7sxbV9k0ntK_hRPq9ES-V48p88R1mNRqNIhlQTEY6Q9WQBabs4MJOUL-JQ2thaaoYv0A9AMVp8ghASJ-kgDoemCj_uk4c14vqXI-L9GN5VeIhk2QjSMLhc4KVJfLNT00aWFYtuE2C_c5MO-oAJHcVCy1JkfsI610m5uReTf-DAT5pWrLHRxell3V2QtpCFG-mAdks44g7Bn92TxEOcqvWjWpCm1scRtIiNvWKcQAj2v4zCXV7ud1xCLfw60iGbmKB6vPAvM8_2EQUgEomGaD4Q-H7ZGLpB4PkLrPEWBtHpoKjlSqe24Pw82TsStCK_aOJYgRtHPijDCcFga4j2UYw6gUEgbAaXriwxGpCEGbl3SwvCbKiIfkCtApoPRCI5EbiUHeSxVL_fwVYKWuc7wfqx4pl3kH8syAGbUQTGg7mdAB192JRgRmUnMIcDbTw%3D%3D)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=3beed891c2a140fba52663d2e4c771db&_e=hsFfoH86FbFauDLqY88TtpImgEnmJoMmWcrgA-KUCo53DkkLDAl4z2hpXXIKJDJjZVhSXTm1G1IC_6_YDktZJqI775qIDtTXljsjDkOjlb4FRH09PpmlT3pJifWOqMwm1kMSORhj09wR9GHyYnrE6_HC7gxAed4s4qmrIqOhjgZGvpTJt6xBo_xf2fAhNoiN2Pf13cERYXXRlUL01_1NwauizsHp9NTcHhc6-rTq6-p3b0PLHUNGqNv95UcHE23UusfLQjH1dzI-r8jIxkRsqz9K-xDbhZihUSIaFI6aJQNQVKj2gYqymBpzS7JIzBmfBgWlfbgaUiUCYZMqV7gqU-pn6wFYhnDwDH5qUT2w1uWiNE8oxHxVPonjCrTrX91483ssmH7Rlg9fEjXVULuDzBI4hg3ygrHMK0V84qZ3uJRVW4FdKFGTgl8AlenGwHsWPP0c2oIXT2566dinAagOdoDzvExidzHeE6RDhlm6muxP8DOEbfDauyobU4AHdOdvuXPTXR6H3zPgnnDrr994Dy1qtSCEfpm8k5Fu3BQzm6IqJpH5S_rQkW6f4gU3s_RsluqkEwpP_8niwh1d7ho1EzdcVybLmFSHdEiSILPcYS6YK91o7Ll7zY2mhYlaBgu2fEbdQqyHono5hiDVV00cUDeRX6HW2xEawPutyLFJMSBlfgC_z81HLurI61hQ7JdXVZgNGn4UFdX2eBWeWXW7_w%3D%3D)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

| | Dear Patriot,

They couldn’t stop you from driving your car.

They couldn’t ban your gas stove.

They couldn’t ram through their “net zero” fantasies.

So now they’re coming at you from every other angle they can find.

I’m Craig Rucker, President of **CFACT – the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow** – and I want to give you a frank update on what the United Nations is actually up to right now.

Because it’s not just one thing. It’s everything.

Right now, unelected UN bureaucrats are pushing a sprawling agenda designed to control how you heat your home, what you drive, what you eat, what products you can buy, and how much you pay for all of it.

The Plastics Treaty. Agenda 2030. “Sustainable consumption” frameworks. “Loss and damage” wealth transfers.

Different labels. Same playbook. Same target – your wallet, your freedom, and your way of life.

Your gas stove is a “carbon threat.” Your pickup truck is “unsustainable.” Your grocery packaging is “an environmental crisis.”

| | | _(Already taken this action?[Go here for more](https://default.salsalabs.org/T282b2842-a5d6-4d63-8805-21015ece6fa6/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9))_ Donald Trump had no right to force his name onto the Kennedy Center, and a judge has ordered that it be removed. **[So why the hell is it still up on the Kennedy Center web site?](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta4157234-0a48-4340-86c7-70677db3e95f/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Look, we get that making physical changes to the building -- making and adding new signs, etc., cannot be done in an instant. But the web site? That should take about 5 minutes. Get the old files that were there before, and put them back. And if they need help, they’d have plenty of volunteers. Every second his name stays up there is a chance for people around the globe to be appalled, and for our Village Idiot to steal the spotlight from the performers. And if Trump or his board supporters are blocking staff from doing it, that needs to end right now. **[Add your name, and tell the Kennedy Center to “Take Trump’s Name off the Kennedy Center web site NOW!”](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7264c3d7-11da-45bb-af54-4c7119acab5c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

Hey folks,
**Adam Mockler** and I jumped in expecting to talk about politics, but we ended up digging into something much bigger: what happens when people in power start treating independent voices as enemies. We talked about fear, media, accountability, and why some of the loudest attacks are actually signs that the other side is losing ground. If you care about democracy, independent media, and where this country is headed.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:05:06**] We break down the Trump administration's new "media offenders" strategy and why targeting creators and journalists is designed to create a chilling effect.
* [**00:11:31**] A deeper conversation about Viktor Orban, Hungary, and why attacks on independent media are often a warning sign of democratic backsliding.
* [**00:17:38**] I share a conversation with my Republican dad--and the simple question that stopped the debate in its tracks.
* [**00:22:39**] We unpack the White House's attacks on creators like David Pakman, Brian Tyler Cohen, and others, and why independent media has become such a threat to those in power.
* [**00:29:05**] We close with a reminder of what actually makes independent media possible: you. No billionaires. No special interests. Just people showing up and supporting the work.

This conversation is about more than one website or one political fight. It's about whether independent voices can continue to challenge powerful institutions when those institutions start pushing back. We talked about media consolidation, executive power, political accountability, and why grassroots-supported creators matter now more than ever. If you've been looking for a clear-eyed conversation about what's happening--and what we can do about it--this is an essential listen. If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.

--Mike

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

3. Passing Medicare for All

money groups have already launched over $9.8 million dollars’ worth of ads
opposing us.

That’s why I need your help right now. The people have overcome big money

stick together.

name: Aaron Ford
subject: This small business owner cut his own wages to support his employees under the failed Lombardo-Trump economy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=251%2E127862%2EqAnrkl)
A few weeks ago, I walked into a grocery store on the Westside of North Las Vegas and met with the owner, Mario.
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260607_1_ak.tkgNAj&amount=5&refcode=em20260607-238&t=2&akid=251%2E127862%2EqAnrkl)_Credit: Jeff Scheid/The Nevada Independent_
Mario has been running this store for years. He knows his customers by name. He cares about his neighborhood. He's doing everything right.
But the Lombardo-Trump economy is making it nearly impossible for Mario to stay afloat. The cost of basic goods for his store has skyrocketed. Sales were down at one of his locations.
To keep their employees paid, Mario and his partner cut their own wages.
**This is what the Lombardo-Trump economy looks like on a personal level.**
I've already taken the Trump administration to court over the tariffs that are driving up costs for small business owners like Mario. And as governor, I'll keep fighting.
But I need your help to get there.

Aaron

body:
A tradition I’ve carried with me
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Where I’m from, the Rio Grande Valley, we’re very family-oriented — and we like to eat _a lot_!
In our household, conversations are always accompanied by some sweet bread, some coffee, or a huge meal. **Cooking has always been our favorite way to connect with family and show our love, and it’s a tradition I still carry with me.**
But these days, with the campaign ramping up and my schedule being jam-packed, I hardly have time to make a delicious, home-cooked meal for my family anymore.
But when _I do_ manage to get into the kitchen,**I always make a dish that’s a true South Texas staple passed down through my family — calabaza con pollo (chicken and squash).**
It’s a hearty, comforting Mexican dish, and the best part is that you can make this a single serving or feed a crowd.
I wanted to do something special today to share a piece of my home with you. For everyone who pitches in to support our grassroots movement, I’ll send along my personal calabaza con pollo recipe with your donation receipt.
**[Peter, will you chip in $5 or any amount today to get the recipe?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260607_2_recipe.SxMqOC&refcode=em20260607-1285&amount=5&t=1&akid=1285%2E299639%2EtXD2Rx)**

**Kristina Knickerbocker** , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school.

**Sarah Trone Garriott** , running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, is a minister, a mom, and the daughter of a nurse and an auto mechanic who worked at Walmart, waited tables, and cleaned hotel rooms to pay for college.

**Kaela Berg** , running for Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District, is a union flight attendant who has worked multiple jobs at once.

**Rebecca Cooke** , running to flip Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, is a longtime waitress and daughter of dairy farmers who still takes diner shifts between campaign stops.

**Keisha Lance Bottoms** , running to flip the Georgia governor’s office, is a fifth-generation Georgian, mom of four, and former Atlanta mayor who is fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families across Georgia.

**Deb Haaland** , running for governor of New Mexico, is a single mom who relied on food stamps and sold homemade salsa to make ends meet while raising her daughter.

**_And then there are the badass women who have already served their country in uniform — and are now stepping up to keep serving in office:_**

**JoAnna Mendoza** , running to flip Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, served in the Navy and Marine Corps. **Rebecca Bennett** , running to flip New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, is a former Navy helicopter pilot.

**Jessica Killin** , running to flip Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, served as an Army captain and paratrooper. **Leela Gray** , running to flip Florida’s 13th Congressional District, is a retired Army brigadier general. **Nancy Lacore** , running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, worked her way through the Naval ranks to eventually serve as the Chief of the Navy Reserve, entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors.

These women have served their country. They have worked for a paycheck. They have cared for their families and communities. And now, they are running to represent people whose lives reflect the same struggles they’ve experienced firsthand.

This is why electing women matters so much this cycle, Peter.

The women EMILYs List supports are not running because politics is easy. They are running because their communities need leaders who understand what working families are actually up against — and who are ready to fight for them.

But even the strongest candidates cannot win alone.

clean_body: | = We knew that would get your attention. Now, Peter, let us introduce you to a few women who should have it instead. Women who are veterans. Women who have working-class backgrounds. Women who are caregivers, small business owners, public servants, and leaders. They know what it means to stretch a dollar, make hard choices, serve their communities, and fight for the people counting on them. That is not just a compelling biography. It is a strong electoral strategy. Democrats need candidates who can speak directly to voters who feel ignored, squeezed, and written off. = | = Kristina Knickerbocker , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school. Sarah Trone Garriott , running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, is a minister, a mom, and the daughter of a nurse and an auto mechanic who worked at Walmart, waited tables, and cleaned hotel rooms to pay for college. Kaela Berg , running for Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District, is a union flight attendant who has worked multiple jobs at once. Rebecca Cooke , running to flip Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, is a longtime waitress and daughter of dairy farmers who still takes diner shifts between campaign stops. Keisha Lance Bottoms , running to flip the Georgia governor’s office, is a fifth-generation Georgian, mom of four, and former Atlanta mayor who is fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families across Georgia. Deb Haaland , running for governor of New Mexico, is a single mom who relied on food stamps and sold homemade salsa to make ends meet while raising her daughter. And then there are the badass women who have already served their country in uniform — and are now stepping up to keep serving in office: JoAnna Mendoza , running to flip Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, served in the Navy and Marine Corps. Rebecca Bennett , running to flip New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, is a former Navy helicopter pilot. Jessica Killin , running to flip Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, served as an Army captain and paratrooper. Leela Gray , running to flip Florida’s 13th Congressional District, is a retired Army brigadier general. Nancy Lacore , running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, worked her way through the Naval ranks to eventually serve as the Chief of the Navy Reserve, entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors. These women have served their country. They have worked for a paycheck. They have cared for their families and communities. And now, they are running to represent people whose lives reflect the same struggles they’ve experienced firsthand. This is why electing women matters so much this cycle, Peter. The women EMILYs List supports are not running because politics is easy. They are running because their communities need leaders who understand what working families are actually up against — and who are ready to fight for them. They aren’t just titles to me.

| | | | | | [A Mom, Navy Wife, Navy Veteran, Nurse Practitioner, & Congresswoman.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNjA3X0pQLVFXLjExMDExN190MTkxOTk5Mi0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDYwN19KUC1RVy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MTk5OTItMjA2OCJ9/gHTfN8Tna_iUZIR6jaxu6A)
Those are the many hats I’ve worn over my life.
I wear these hats proudly every day, but they aren’t just titles to me. They’re the perspectives I bring with me to Washington.
* Mom & Navy Wife: protector, trying to create a better world for the next generation,
* Navy Veteran: mission-focused leader, someone who knows how to get the job done under pressure,
* Nurse Practitioner: caregiver, someone who listens first and works to heal systems that so often are broken.

I didn’t head to Washington to hear myself talk on the evening news and preach broken promises. I ran for office because I was sick and tired of the broken promises.
[I refused to be a bystander while our community’s needs went unmet.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNjA3X0pQLVFXLjExMDExN190MTkxOTk5Mi0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDYwN19KUC1RVy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MTk5OTItMjA2OCJ9/ll4nxNGtpIqAsFSQN5lf5g)
They say if you want something done right, you’ve got to do it yourself.
That’s why I’m on the front lines in Washington fighting for American citizens like you, Peter.
I don’t rely on high-dollar donors, unlike my opponent, who has the backing of all the far-Left millionaire mega-donors. I rely on folks like you who believe that service is a solo act, not a photo op.
The radical Left is trying to shut my lights off; they don’t want a conservative Mother, Veteran, and Nurse Practitioner to succeed.
We can’t let them take control; we need to hold the line together.

subject: What happened back in 2016
body:
10,000 votes 10 years ago
|
